chunks: The Children of Israel, when a drop of urine would touch one of them, would cut their flesh with scissors. But Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has granted you expansive ease, wider than what is between the heaven and the earth, and has made water purifying for you. So observe how you conduct yourselves.

key_terms.بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ: The Children of Israel, cited as a historical comparison
key_terms.بِالْمَقَارِيضِ: With scissors, indicating the severity of their former practice
key_terms.طَهُورًا: Purifying; that which cleanses ritual impurity
key_terms.فَانْظُرُوا: So consider; a call to reflect and be mindful
key_terms.قَطْرَةُ بَوْلٍ: A drop of urine, referring to ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Allah’s leniency in the laws of ritual purity for this Ummah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام contrasts the severity placed upon Banū Isrāʾīl in matters of impurity with the ease Allah has granted this Ummah through the purifying function of water. The hadith teaches both the ruling-related significance of taharah and an ethical reminder to appreciate and properly uphold Allah’s facilitation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.13 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The Children of Israel, if a drop of urine touched them, they would cut away the affected flesh with scissors. But Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted, has granted you vast leniency—wider than the space between the heavens and the earth—and has made water purifying for you. So, consider how you conduct yourselves (at removing impurities)”.
